meta.title: Research & Analysis catalog
meta.method: One list of what the Research & Analysis page (insights.html) shows. Each entry holds metadata and a link only: no figures. How an item is kept current is its maintenance: "reviewed" items take their check and review dates from the data file named in review_from, so the dates live in one place; "dated" items are published once and not updated, so they show their publication date; "generated" items are rebuilt from the repository whenever it changes; "live-data" pages render from data files and show those files' vintages themselves. Curated research briefs are listed from data/policy_briefs_curated.json and are not repeated here.

sections.label: Current policy status
sections.note: Checked against official sources on a schedule. A review badge appears when a check is due.

sections.label: Analysis and research briefs
sections.note: Dated pieces, newest first. They are not updated after publication; the date says how current they are.

sections.label: Papers and methods
sections.note: COHO's own method, written up and regenerated from the repository.

sections.label: Data explorations
sections.note: Pages that render from COHO's data files. Each shows the vintage of the data it uses.

entries.title: Policy & Legislation
entries.summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) became law July 11, 2026; the enacted text is a housing-supply and HUD-program reform law and does not include the LIHTC cap expansion described in earlier versions. Also the tax-credit policy watchlist and the Colorado policy watch.

entries.title: Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act (AHCIA)
entries.summary: Two AHCIA provisions, the 12% Housing Credit ceiling increase and the 25% bond test, became law in July 2025. The rest of the bill is pending as H.R. 2725 and S. 1515; their status is read from the watchlist.

entries.title: Fair Housing Without the Rulebook
entries.summary: The Fair Housing Act was not repealed and disparate-impact claims still exist under Inclusive Communities. What has been dismantled is the administrative machinery, and HUD's Title VI proposal takes public comment until 9 October 2026.

entries.title: Colorado Housing Costs: County-Level Analysis
entries.summary: County maps of rent and price change over 10- and 15-year windows, with a drivers-of-change model for all 64 Colorado counties, built from ACS, FHFA HPI, BLS and Census building permits.

entries.title: CRA Expansion Impact on LIHTC Pricing
entries.summary: What LIHTC pricing could do if Community Reinvestment Act rules widened the investor base. These are scenarios with author-estimated probabilities, not forecasts: no such expansion is enacted or pending. The actual CRA rule status is in the watchlist.

entries.title: Instrumenting Housing Need
entries.summary: How this system learned to say "we don't know", and why a coerced zero misallocates as well as misinforms: the place-level method, the apportionment and PITI decisions, a worked jurisdiction, and what is still missing.

entries.title: Deciding About Housing With Public Data
entries.summary: A plain-language companion to the working paper for planners: what the evidence can and cannot establish, with a worked Colorado example.

entries.title: What the Numbers Actually Do
entries.summary: The full computational specification: tract-to-place apportionment, the ACS household anchor, cost burden, the ownership affordability models, the scoring chain and the absence rules. Every constant is read from the file that defines it.

entries.title: Tax Credit Equity Markets
entries.summary: LIHTC equity pricing history, Novogradac national and regional benchmarks, transfer-credit pricing, and the federal policy watchlist, all rendered from data files.

entries.title: LIHTC Basics
entries.summary: A practical guide for developers, housing authorities and investors: development timelines, financing structures, QAP strategy and due diligence.

entries.title: Help for Homebuyers
entries.summary: Plain-language cards for Colorado and federal homebuyer credits, grants, down-payment assistance and property-tax relief, from source-linked program data.

entries.title: Colorado Affordable Housing Market Analysis
entries.summary: County-level maps and tables: DDAs and QCTs with LIHTC projects, income-band gaps, concessions, foreclosures and Proposition 123 commitments.

entries.title: Colorado Market Intelligence
entries.summary: Statewide demand and supply signals, affordable inventory and a policy landscape, rendered from COHO's data files.

entries.title: Historical Trends & Benchmarks
entries.summary: What past LIHTC deals in Colorado looked like: CHFA awards by year and credit type, the LIHTC stock over time, and peer project benchmarks.
